preamble: The GOAT diphthong [oʊ] reduces to schwa [ə] in unstressed final syllables in many nonstandard varieties of English. Final unstressed -ow is reduced to schwa and conflated with the -er/-ar ending (rhotic [ɚ] in rhotic accents), as dialect forms and pronunciation spellings such as feller 'fellow', winder 'window', yeller 'yellow' and Appalachian holler 'hollow' show. Careful standard speech keeps a full or reduced rounded vowel ([oʊ], [ɵ]) in these words. No equivalent change has been verified outside English.
